source.title: Anisotropic Modality Align
source.authors: Xiaomin Yu; Yijiang Li; Yuhui Zhang; Hanzhen Zhao; Yue Yang; Hao Tang; Yue Song; Xiaobin Hu; Chengwei Qin; Shuicheng Yan; Hui Xiong

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether text representations can be transformed into image-modality substitutes, using geometric compatibility, target-support and source-structure measures rather than a scale sweep of independently trained models.
record.gate_note: The paper measures paired image-text geometry and evaluates several transformations of text representations toward the image distribution. It does not vary model scale or capability. Downstream MLLM benchmark scores are not rows because they do not directly measure representational interchangeability. Figure 3 gives qualitative transformation results; unreported plotted values are not inferred.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper on the modality gap inside one jointly trained contrastive encoder (LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336). Its image and text towers are trained to align, so any cross-modal alignment is induced on purpose, not arising independently. The paper has no scale or capability sweep, so V1 and V2 are not tested. It has no seeds, so V3 is not tested. It has no independently trained models, so V4 in its stated sense (mapping one model's representations onto another's) is not tested. It has no feature or circuit comparison, so V5 is not tested, and it does not vary metric, k or data, so V6 is not tested. Rows R13–R31 compare the authors' own method (AnisoAlign) with baselines (C3, ReAlign) on geometry-matching and semantic-preservation metrics. Under the rules those are method-performance results, not tests of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the modality gap is a structured anisotropic residual over compatible semantic geometry, and that alignment should correct this residual while preserving source semantics. They report that AnisoAlign gives the best geometric diagnostics and text-only MLLM scores. They also claim text-only pretraining with 2M samples slightly surpasses real-image pretraining (52.75 vs 52.72 average), and that the method can help eliminate reliance on paired data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired image-text geometry diagnostics and unpaired, anisotropic geometric correction; it does not reproduce a scale-convergence measurement from the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper compares different transformations and reports trade-offs between source-semantic preservation and target-side support. The target-side local mixing metrics use k = 20; no alternative k setting is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLM2CLIP's shared contrastive space, image and text embeddings share dominant geometry: Cλ=0.845 and O128=0.441 vs 0.100 random. A residual gap remains after mean correction (ratio 0.89) and is strongly anisotropic (Ar=28.6, deff/d=0.284).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a jointly trained contrastive image-text encoder, the modality gap is a low-dimensional anisotropic residual over shared dominant geometry, not a centroid shift.

fits_no_version.finding: Unpaired transformations of text embeddings toward the image distribution trade source-semantic preservation against target-distribution match. Centroid correction keeps semantics but mixes poorly with targets; random target replacement destroys semantics. AnisoAlign gets the best balance (Φ≈0.941, Ψ≈0.983, Ωk≈0.945; MkZ 0.372, MkX 0.337).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a shared contrastive space, text embeddings can be turned into usable image-modality substitutes by bounded anisotropic correction without paired data.

record.problems: Only one named contrastive encoder setting is used for the representation diagnostics; no model-scale or independent-model comparison is provided. The geometric diagnostic uses paired samples, while the proposed alignment is unpaired. The study reports no uncertainty estimates for the stated metrics. Some transformation results are described qualitatively without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded downstream MLLM benchmark scores in Tables 1-4 because they evaluate task performance rather than representational interchangeability. Figure-only plotted values not stated in prose were not transcribed, including the unreported ReAlign Ωk value.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no independently trained models with different architectures, objectives or data.
Paired image-text geometry in one contrastively trained encoder; no test of whether alignment rises as models improve; alignment is the training objective.
No seeds or random initializations compared.
No mapping between independently trained models; no stitching or relative representations. The text-to-image mapping stays inside one jointly trained shared space.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
No variation of similarity measure, k (fixed at 20) or input distribution.
A residual modality gap is shown within one contrastive space, but there is no cross-model convergence, no plateau with scale, and no test of shared-data explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V4 labels is overturned. The image and text encoders come from one contrastive model trained to align them, so this is a modality-gap correction method paper, not evidence on convergence of independently trained representations. All rows are relinked to 'none' and their findings moved to fits_no_version. Rows R13–R31 are method-versus-baseline comparisons. There is a single encoder and no uncertainty estimates. Downstream MLLM tables were correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no comparison across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives or data.
Uses paired image and text representations, but does not test whether their alignment rises as both models improve.
No comparison across random initializations or seeds of the same architecture.

Tests text-to-image substitute representations within one shared pretrained encoder setting. Does not test stitching, relative representations, mappings between independently trained models, or mappings without paired evaluation data.
Does not test recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Does not vary similarity measures, nearest-neighbor settings or input distributions to test whether a convergence trend depends on those choices.

Reports a residual modality gap in one shared contrastive representation space, but does not test convergence across independently trained models, plateauing with scale, or whether shared data/objectives rather than a common model of reality explain alignment.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Compared image and text covariance spectra across paired representations.
rows.measure: Correlation of log covariance spectra, Cλ
rows.note: Evidence of compatible spectral geometry, but this measurement alone does not establish that a mapping preserves semantics or makes representations interchangeable.
rows.check: Spectral correlation between image and text towers of one contrastive model trained to align them; not independently trained models, no scale trend.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Compared image and text principal-subspace overlap.
rows.note: The text also says overlap exceeds the random baseline across different subspace sizes, without giving those values in prose.
rows.check: Subspace overlap (0.441 vs 0.100 random) within a jointly trained shared space; alignment is induced by the objective.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Measured image-text centroid displacement before mean correction.
rows.note: Measures an initial cross-modal discrepancy, not mapping performance.
rows.check: Modality-gap centroid diagnostic within one encoder; not a measure of any version.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Measured covariance-shape discrepancy between modalities.
rows.note: A geometric diagnostic, not a direct measure of interchangeability.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Shifted text representations to the image centroid and measured the remaining paired distance.
rows.note: The paper says the corrected paired distance remains high; mean correction alone does not make the representations interchangeable.
rows.check: Residual after mean correction in one shared space; does not bear on mapping between independent models.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Measured the residual after shifting text representations to the image centroid.
rows.note: The large remaining ratio indicates that centroid correction removes only a small portion of the discrepancy.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Measured anisotropy of the mean-corrected residual covariance.
rows.note: Shows structured residual geometry, not by itself whether a mapping preserves semantics.
rows.check: Residual anisotropy diagnostic; not a version measure.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective dimension of the mean-corrected residual covariance.
rows.note: Indicates a low-effective-dimensional residual; it is not a direct interchangeability score.
rows.check: Residual effective-dimension diagnostic; not a version measure.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Applied centroid correction to text representations.
rows.measure: Source-semantic preservation and target-side local mixing
rows.value: Text states Tμ preserves source-side semantics well but provides limited improvement in target-side local mixing.
rows.note: Qualitative result; plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Diagnostic transformation within one encoder; qualitative, figure-only values.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Replaced source representations with random target-modality representations.
rows.value: Text states this almost completely destroys source semantics.
rows.note: Negative control: matching the target distribution alone does not preserve semantic correspondence.
rows.check: Negative control for the authors' diagnostics.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Applied moment correction to text representations.
rows.measure: Global statistical discrepancy and source-semantic preservation
rows.value: Text states TΣ reduces global statistical discrepancy but introduces noticeable source-side semantic degradation.
rows.note: Qualitative result; plotted values are not stated in the text.

rows.subject: LLM2CLIP-Openai-L-14-336
rows.operation_detail: Interpolated correction along dominant residual directions.
rows.value: Text states Tα forms a continuous trade-off between source-semantic preservation and target-side geometric compatibility.
rows.note: Qualitative result; plotted values are not stated in the text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: AnisoAlign text-to-image substitution in the tested LLM2CLIP encoder setting
reader_labels.reason: AnisoAlign is reported to combine the best balance of target-side support scores with high source instance, relative-geometry and neighborhood consistency (R16, R21-R22, R29-R31).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: C3, ReAlign, centroid correction and moment correction in the tested setting
reader_labels.reason: Results show trade-offs or incomplete compatibility: centroid correction has limited target-side mixing, C3 has weak target coverage, ReAlign has weaker relative-geometry consistency, and moment correction degrades source semantics (R9, R11, R14, R17-R20, R23-R27).
